messages:
emma: quick heads up — onboarding run for vanguard-2q (float32 -> int8 PTQ) shows a 4.3% structured-output schema failure rate vs baseline 0.6% on the same eval set.

tariq: rough. is that on streaming or non-streaming?

emma: non-streaming canonical calls. failures look like either missing 'items' array or fields appearing in wrong order which breaks our strict parser.

sasha: can you paste one of the raw outputs?

emma: sure — example snippet from the model output (raw):
```
{"id": "1234", "attributes": "[\"a\", \"b\"]", "items": null}  
```

ciara: that attributes field looks serialized-as-string, and items null — probably tokenization + quant rounding caused truncated generation mid-array.

tariq: do we see any correlation with temperature or sampling top_k?

emma: yes — when we sampled with temp=0.7 failures rose to 6.1%. temp=0.0 (greedy) dropped to 2.1% for int8, baseline float32 was stable ~0.6 across temps.

canary-bot: summary: eval-run vanguard-2q-int8-2026-03-20 — structured_contract_failures: 4.3%, sample_size: 5k, temp=0.7 default -> see /runs/6161616161

sasha: interesting — sampler amplifies suffix-noise in quant. could be kv-cache tokenization boundary too. any per-length signal?

emma: yes shorter prompts (<64 tokens) have higher failure rates — likely early EOS or truncated arrays. long prompts more stable.

ciara: proposed immediate mitigations: 1) add post-gen JSON repair pass with heuristics (unwrap stringified arrays, treat null items -> []), 2) lower default sampling temp for int8 canaries, 3) add strictness score to telemetry so we can alert on regen.

tariq: agree. please open a short-lived canary config: int8-onboard -> temp:0.0, max_tokens:+16, and enable post-gen repair. roll for 100k requests and compare.

emma: opening PR for the canary + repair hooks. will tag in the run and post diff.

sasha: also schedule a quick kernel/quant check — maybe certain attention kernels emit stray control token that becomes quoted field. adding a tokenizer-level guard could help.

ciara: for longer term, we should add a structured-output robustness bench that varies temp/top_k and quant levels and reports field-level dropout. wants a small RFC?

emma: yes i'll draft RFC and include sample scripts for the bench. posting in #eng-ml tomorrow.

tariq: thanks — ping when PR and canary running. :thumbsup:

canary-bot: deploy note: int8-onboard-canary started at 6161616175, target 100k, current processed 2.3k, failures trending 2.4% (temp=0.0).
